01 / EXPERIMENT

Shared inputs, visible advantages

Loading recorded evaluations…

16 scenes: four LibriSpeech test speakers × requested RT60 0 / 0.3 s × input SNR 0 / 5 dB. Each speaker has one assigned geometry and one three-second utterance. Speaker and geometry are confounded. The clean reference is the target's room-filtered ear image, not dry speech.

All hearing-metric outputs receive the same exact NAL-R fitting and digital ceiling, with the same sloping audiogram [10, 15, 25, 40, 55, 60] dB HL at [250, 500, 1000, 2000, 4000, 6000] Hz. SI-SDR and spatial diagnostics are measured before fitting. No independent output loudness normalization.

Information access is not matched

Classical MVDR receives one second of target-muted noise calibration. “Known” steering also receives the true target angle. Estimated steering uses microphone mixtures. The neural hybrid uses learned masks with future context and whole-utterance statistics, without clean stems or true DOA. These are exploratory measurements, not a causal SOTA leaderboard or clinical validation.

02 / QUALITY & DISTORTION

Compare by condition

MethodHASPI ↑HASQI ↑SI-SDR dB ↑ILD error dB ↓ITD error μs ↓Rows

Averages: ears within scene, conditions within speaker, then speakers. HASPI/HASQI range 0–1; they are predictions, not observed word scores or MOS. ILD/ITD errors compare output mixtures against clean target images; ITD resolution is 62.5 μs. They are not human localization error. ↑/↓ show preferred direction, not clinical pass limits.

MethodHASPI speaker rangeHASQI speaker rangeTarget-only SI-SDR dBTarget level change dBOutput level change dB

Speaker ranges describe this small sample; they are not confidence intervals. Target-only decomposition is available only for fixed linear methods. A separate neural run on clean speech does not decompose its mixture output. Level changes prevent scale-invariant SI-SDR from hiding target attenuation.

04 / LOCALIZATION

Direction is not identity

TestMicsSector ±°Mean error °Within 10°Accepted updatesFirst accepted after step ms

Separate waveform-based free-field tests with speech: front, rear, a direction step at 2 s, and a louder interferer. Sector centre is 0°; ±90° intentionally excludes the rear target. Two microphones have a front/back ambiguity. The gate accepts peak contrast ≥0.02; it is not a probability. Step timing is the first accepted correct estimate, not sustained settling time. Raw traces and protocol.

05 / COMPUTE, MEMORY & DELAY

Offline throughput is not streaming latency

The live array has 10.67 ms STFT delay. RNNoise adds 30 ms in the pinned adapter. Localization adds no audio queue but uses 100 ms smoothing and 21.33 ms updates. The offline neural model uses a bidirectional LSTM and full-utterance statistics; it has no finite live latency claim.

06 / VERSION 0.5

Choosing the talker, closing the loop

Steering controllers on full simulated waveforms (MVDR; delay-and-sum for the crossing case). SNR gain is left-ear output SNR relative to the unsteered front pair. Lock-on is told the target direction once at t = 0; dominant and speech-like controllers get no direction. Method · JSON

ScenarioControllerSNR gain (dB)Mean error (°)Within 10°Steered nearer masker

Closed-loop feedback simulation of the browser engine (4 ms forward delay). Maximum stable path gain in dB, swept from −40 to +10 dB; “+10 (edge)” means no failure was found inside the sweep. Level change is the wanted-sound change over the last 5 s at −20 dB path gain. Synthetic path: upper bounds for the model, not device results. Method · JSON
